caption:
Save this list for your next Halifax trip! We stayed downtown Halifax during our last visit and there are so many great activities for toddlers + kids! The best part is we could walk to all of these spots within 15 minutes from our hotel. I did a bit of research before going, so you don’t have to ♥️ Aurelia absolutely loved Halifax, all the activities and even the seafood 🦞 
-
📍Sea Turtle Centre at the Salt yard is a great spot to learn about sea turtles, do some crafting and draw with chalk. Aurelia made 2 very lovely jellyfish 🪼 here and spent a looooooong time drawing with chalk outside. FREE to visit and craft.
📍The Halifax Public Library, where there’s an entire floor dedicated to kids. We spent 2 mornings here during our visit because it was just so much fun! There’s a whole toddler area with toys, puzzles and more. A secondary soft block and balance beam area and then a Lego table for slightly older kids. Bonus points that it’s a FREE activity and that there’s a coffee shop on the top floor with incredible views of the water 🌊 
📍Maritime museum of the Atlantic, open everyday 9:30am-4:30pm (except for Tuesdays, when it’s FREE ✨ to visit 4-8PM). Explore shipbuilding, naval exhibits and kids play areas! Adults are $5.15-11, kids $3-6.50 and kids 5 and under are FREE ✨ 
📍Yellow submarine playground on the waterfront is a fun spot too! If you’re just looking to fill some time because it can get quite busy. 
📍The Discovery Centre is open everyday 9am-4pm and perfect for kids to learn about the Ocean, Flying, Energy, the body and play in the themed areas on the top floor (where there’s also a cafe and eating area). We spent 2 days exploring the centre because there was so much to do! Adults are $17.50+ tax, kids $14.50 + tax and a family 4 pass is $58 + tax, 2 and under are free ✨ 
*Aurelia also loved watching for boats by the waterfront and we didn’t get to explore the HMCS Sackville nor the CSS Acadia but those are also good options to explore. 
-
Am I missing any key activities for kids? Let me know or share your favourites! ♥️ #halifaxkids #halifaxnovascotia #halifaxwaterfront #halifaxns #maritimemuseum

We went last weekend and parked before 9AM around Dow’s Lake and walked over (with our stroller). At least, not until I told her we were going to get a snack and drink at @morningowlparkdale ♥️
-
If you’re parking 🚗 near Dow’s Lake, I highly recommend getting there earlier and finding a spot to park along Rochester or Beech st (Beech also has a great parking lot across from Almanac grain). Anywhere in little Italy with street parking or a lot works, depending on how far you want to walk. If you’re looking for parking lots downtown, maybe send me a DM! Alright friends, here’s a full recap on my very first chemical peel with @skinspaesthetics ♥️ Previously, I’ve had a Oxygeneo facial and a photo facial with Skin Spa Esthetics. They recommended a chemical peel to really target my pigmentation and uneven skin tone. And if you’ve ever seen chemical peel recovery videos, they can be aggressive but they can also be gentler. Let’s break it down together. 
1. Full skin consultation with analysis to determine your target areas (this was really cool)
2. The double cleanse to get the skin ready for the chemical peel itself, which was a very soothing experience. 
3. The Chemical peel itself (clear gel like substance), is applied and it stays on for a little while to really target the outer layer of the skin.
3. Clean off the peel and apply a refreshing face mask.
4. Apply lotion and sunscreen, which is ideal when recovering from a chemical peel because your skin will be very sensitive. 
5. Wait a few days to see the peel’s full effect. I experience a bit of tightness, itchiness and some dry skin. But once all of this goes away, my skin is brother and clearer! 
-
SO, if you’re interested in trying out a chemical peel at @skinspaesthetics then mention OLIVIA when booking to save $50 off your chemical peel (for the entire month of January). caption:
Ottawa, if you haven’t been to the @canwarmuseum then you need to plan a visit! The museum tells the story of Canada’s military past through interactive exhibits, artifacts, personal stories, artwork, and photos. You’ll find every exhibit has a lot to explore and a lot of interactive aspects to each space. Walk through mock trenches, read/listen to stories, explore the Lebreton Gallery with tanks, cars and more! You’ll even be able to take in the unique architecture of the building during your visit. 
-
Grab a bite to eat at the cafeteria, take in the scenic views from the outdoor patio or visit the gift shop! There’s also board games in the Lebreton gallery to keep the little ones busy (board games and life sized chess/connect 4). All summer long, take advantage of the Canada Strong Pass where children 17 and under are free and youth (18-24) receive a 50% discount on admission. Make it both an educational and fun trip for the family!

Ottawa parents, if you haven’t been to the @scitechmuseum then you absolutely need to visit! It’s such an excellent spot for a day of fun-filled learning for all ages. -
2 and under are always free. But take advantage of the Canada Strong pass this summer for free admission for 17 and under, and 50% off for 18-24!

As a first time mom, the transition to daycare was new to me. The uncertainty of when our baby would eat, sleep, or drink milk. I wondered if she was being soothed or comforted, if upset. But, we had toured the daycare centre and kept in contact with the program director. We knew the schedule and understood that it would take some time to adjust.

Tears were shed the first few weeks, on both baby and mommy’s side. It was odd going from spending everyday with our girl, to only seeing her for an hour before and 2-3 hrs after daycare. On top of returning to work and trying to figure out drop off, pick up and commuting into the office. Add to that, the transition from 2 to 1 nap and our schedules were all jumbled up. Sleep is choppy and everyone is a bit tired. 
-
Fast forward 2 months and everything is falling into place. No more tears are shed, only tears of joy. We’ve found somewhat of a rhythm with drop offs and pick ups. And most importantly, our girl is thriving and she’s grown so much! When she started daycare, she didn’t eat many solids, didn’t walk and didn’t really talk much. Now she’s accomplished all of those milestones, spent ample time outdoors, painted, read books + sang songs with her peers and so much more. Knowing that she’s finally settled in makes my heart full and reinforces that I made the right decision. ♥️
